content: 1. Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid can reduce the levels of tetracycline by binding to cations in the gastrointestinal tract. To avoid magnesium chelation, tetracycline should be taken at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after the administration of these agents. Monitor closely. 2. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If necessary, limit the use of the CYP3A4 inhibitor to less than 14 days and monitor for adverse effects, particularly musculoskeletal reactions. 3. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dosage adjustment is required, but regular monitoring of blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function is recommended when sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, may alter the effects of tetracycline. Monitor closely for increased or decreased effects of CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol, as dosage adjustments may be necessary. 5. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. When co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the starting dose of suvorexant to 5 mg at bedtime. 7. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce tadalafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and the risk of adverse events. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Tecovirimat, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor the effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates when co-administered. 10. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage regimen of tezacaftor if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tetracycline increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No specific dose adjustment is recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. However, reduce the dose of tofacitinib if co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 13. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer tetracycline at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing products to avoid reduced bioavailability. 15. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dose of vardenafil if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 17. Tetracycline increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dose of zanubrutinib to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 19. Zinc decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by binding to cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate the administration of oral tetracycline derivatives and oral zinc salts by at least 2 hours. 20. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Tetracycline increases the effects of antithrombin alfa, antithrombin III, and argatroban through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Tetracycline decreases the levels of atovaquone by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The effect may be minor. 24. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 25. Tetracycline increases the effects of bemiparin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 27. Tetracycline increases the effects of bivalirudin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 28. Colestipol decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Tetracycline increases the effects of dalteparin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 31. Danazol increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 32. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 33. Tetracycline increases the effects of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 34. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 35. Tetracycline increases the effects of fondaparinux through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Tetracycline increases the effects of heparin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 38. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of niacin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 40. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Tetracycline increases the effects of phenindione through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 42. Tetracycline increases the effects of protamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 43. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 44. Tetracycline decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing elimination. The clinical significance is unknown. 45. Sucralfate decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 46. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 47. Tetracycline increases the phototoxicity of verteporfin through pharmacodynamic synergism. Monitor closely for increased phototoxicity. 48. Acitretin and tetracycline are contraindicated due to the risk of increased intracranial pressure. Avoid co-administration. 49. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If necessary, separate administration by 2 hours. 50. Aminolevulinic acid oral and tetracycline increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Do not administer other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid oral for 24 hours during the perioperative period. 51. Tetracycline increases the toxicity of aminolevulinic acid topical through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of photosensitizing drugs may enhance phototoxic reactions during photodynamic therapy. 52. Tetracycline decreases the effects of amoxicillin and ampicillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly. 53. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers can lower exposure to CYP3A4 substrates. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose if necessary. 54. Tetracycline increases the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 55. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce avanafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and the risk of adverse events. The maximum recommended dose of avanafil is 50 mg, not to exceed once every 24 hours for patients taking moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 56. Tetracycline increases the levels of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of avapritinib as per dosage modification guidelines. 57. Tetracycline increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, monitor closely and reduce the dose if required.
